subproblems.title: The top-dimensional current [[G]] = τ(G, 1, e_0∧⋯∧e_{n−1}) of a Borel set G ⊆ ℝⁿ is integer multiplicity
subproblems.statement:
Conventions: ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Hⁿ = μHE[n], Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure. 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) = TestFormOn univ n (smooth n-forms on ℝⁿ with compact support) and 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) = GeometricCurrentOn univ n.

An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U ⊆ ℝ^P is the contract structure IMRep U n:
- M is Borel, M ⊆ U and M is countably n-rectifiable;
- θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable, positive on M, and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U;
- ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n is strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.

R represents T when T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). T is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity T) if some IMRep represents it. e_k = EuclideanSpace.single k 1 for k ∈ Fin n.

Statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let G ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set (MeasurableSet G). Then there is an integer multiplicity current A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) with A(ω) = ∫_G ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ). That is, [[G]] = τ(G, 1, e_0∧⋯∧e_{n−1}) is an integer multiplicity current.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Set (Euclid n)), MeasurableSet G → ∃ A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity A ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, A ω = ∫ x in G, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) x (fun k => EuclideanSpace.single k (1 : ℝ)) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent-supplied proof of dor_lmb_fc_dtop_cube_chain_im. There the cube current [[G]] is IM because (G, 1, e_0∧⋯∧e_{n−1}) is an IMRep. Here that argument is specialised to multiplicity 1 and an arbitrary Borel set G. Book: Simon, Ch. 6, 2.2 and Definition 3.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 192–212 and 733–749).

Tools:
- (IMC)(b): part (b) of the accepted sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub. If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and E ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel, then there are A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U representing A with R'.carrier = M ∩ E, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ξ.
- SimonGMT: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule and countablyRectifiable_range.
- Mathlib: EuclideanSpace.basisFun, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, Basis.span_eq, finrank_top, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, Submodule.top_coe, LipschitzWith.id, Set.range_id, lintegral_one, Measure.restrict_apply_univ, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, IsCompact.measure_lt_top, and ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply with apply_apply.

Route: the parent applies (IMC)(b) with E = ℝⁿ to (G, |b|, sign(b)ξ₀) and needs (IMC)(a) for the tangent spaces of G. Here (IMC)(b) is applied with E = G to the full-space triple (ℝⁿ, 1, ξ₀), whose tangent condition holds at every point. (IMC)(b) itself returns an IMRep with carrier G, so (IMC)(a) is not needed.

Notation: e := (e_0, …, e_{n−1}) with e_k = EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Let ξ₀ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid n) ℝ e ∈ MultiVector n n, so ξ₀(α) = α(e) for every n-covector α (by definition, apply_apply).

1. Unit orientation of ⊤.
   (a) By basisFun_apply, e is the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ of ℝⁿ.
   (b) Hence e is orthonormal (OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal).
   (c) span ℝ (range e) = ⊤, by Basis.span_eq for the underlying basis, whose coercion is e (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis).
   (d) Since ξ₀(α) = α(e) for every α, τ := e witnesses IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₀ ⊤ via the first alternative.
   For n = 0 the family e is empty and ⊤ = ⊥ = {0}; the same argument applies.
2. Approximate tangent space of ℝⁿ. finrank ℝ (⊤ : Submodule ℝ ℝⁿ) = finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n (finrank_top, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and every x ∈ ℝⁿ lies in ⊤. By hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule, the set (⊤ : Set ℝⁿ), which is univ (Submodule.top_coe), satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n univ x ⊤ for every x ∈ ℝⁿ.
3. Rectifiability of ℝⁿ. univ = range(id) (Set.range_id) and id : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id). So univ is countably n-rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_range.
4. Local finiteness. Let K ⊆ ℝⁿ be compact. Then ∫⁻_{univ ∩ K} 1 dHⁿ = Hⁿ(univ ∩ K) = Hⁿ(K) (lintegral_one, Measure.restrict_apply_univ). Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Hence ∫⁻_{univ ∩ K} 1 dHⁿ < ∞.
5. The full-space IMRep. Define R ∈ IMRep univ n by carrier := univ, mult := fun _ => 1 and orient := fun _ => ξ₀. Its fields hold:
   - measurableSet_carrier: univ is Borel;
   - carrier_subset: univ ⊆ univ;
   - rectifiable: by step 3;
   - measurable_mult: the constant multiplicity is measurable;
   - mult_pos: 1 > 0 on univ;
   - locallyIntegrable_mult: by step 4, since the cast of 1 is 1;
   - aestronglyMeasurable_orient: the constant orientation is strongly measurable;
   - orients: for every x ∈ ℝⁿ, hence Hⁿ⌞univ-a.e., Q := ⊤ satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n univ x ⊤ (step 2) and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₀ ⊤ (step 1).
6. Restriction to G. univ ⊆ ℝⁿ is open and G is Borel. So (IMC)(b), applied to R with E := G, gives A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) and an IMRep R' in univ representing A, with R'.carrier = univ ∩ G, R'.mult = (fun _ => 1) and R'.orient = (fun _ => ξ₀). In particular A is integer multiplicity, with witness R'.
7. The action. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ). Since R' represents A, A(ω) = R'.action ω = ∫_{R'.carrier} (R'.mult x : ℝ)·R'.orient x (ω(x)) dHⁿ(x). Rewrite with R'.carrier = univ ∩ G = G, R'.mult x = 1 (cast to (1 : ℝ)) and R'.orient x = ξ₀. Then 1·t = t and ξ₀(ω(x)) = ω(x)(e) give A(ω) = ∫_G ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{n−1}) dHⁿ(x). Together with step 6 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: The standard basis e = basisFun is orthonormal and spans ℝⁿ, so ξ₀ = (α ↦ α(e)) is a unit orientation of ⊤. ℝⁿ = (⊤ : Set) has approximate tangent space ⊤ at every point (hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule).
(ℝⁿ, 1, ξ₀) is an IMRep in ℝⁿ. univ = range id is countably n-rectifiable, and Hⁿ = Lebesgue measure makes ∫⁻_{K} 1 dHⁿ finite on compacts.
(IMC)(b) with E = G yields A represented by (univ ∩ G, 1, ξ₀). So A is IM and A(ω) = ∫_G ω(x)(e) dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Algebra of integer multiplicity currents: zero, mass of integer combinations, finite integer combinations (reuse of the accepted declaration cbr_cc_current_algebra)
subproblems.statement:
Conventions as in the parent: ℝ^P = Euclid P; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n; M_W(X) = X.massOn W; X − Y is the contract subtraction; IsIntegerMultiplicity means represented by an IMRep.

(a) For all P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity.
(b) Let A, B, C ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and p, q ∈ ℤ with A(ω) = p·B(ω) + q·C(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then M_W(A) ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C) in [0, ∞] for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.
(c) Assume that differences of integer multiplicity currents in open domains are integer multiplicity: for all P, n, open U and IM A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), A − B is IM. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, ι a type, F ⊆ ι finite, S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity for every i ∈ F, and m_i ∈ ℤ. Then there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_i·S_i(ω) for all ω, and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{i∈F} |m_i|·M_W(S_i) for every W.

This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_cc_current_algebra (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.closure_compact-a1.current_algebra-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U n)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B C : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (p q : ℤ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, A ω = (p : ℝ) * B ω + (q : ℝ) * C ω) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), A.massOn W ≤ (p.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * B.massOn W + (q.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * C.massOn W) ∧ ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ι : Type) (F : Finset ι) (S : ι → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : ι → ℤ), IsOpen U → (∀ i ∈ F, IsIntegerMultiplicity (S i)) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = ∑ i ∈ F, (m i : ℝ) * S i ω) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), Y.massOn W ≤ ∑ i ∈ F, ((m i).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (S i).massOn W)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5 and Remark 3.2(1) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity). This theorem is reused verbatim, not re-proved.
1. The DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.closure_compact-a1.current_algebra-a1 has status accepted ("all proof gates passed; immutable candidate retained"). Its Lean declaration Submission.cbr_cc_current_algebra passed the comparator with exactly this frozen type, a byte-identical lean_statement (candidate commit 791f7d722ecc7a162afa46e5f9e1dd564f0ce80b, PR #6195). It uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
2. Its accepted proof:
   (a) The IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents 0. The carrier is countably n-rectifiable since Hⁿ(∅) = 0, and every integral over ∅ vanishes.
   (b) If ω is admissible for M_W, then so is −ω, hence |X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X). So A(ω) = pB(ω) + qC(ω) ≤ |p|M_W(B) + |q|M_W(C) for every admissible ω, and the bound follows by taking the supremum.
   (c) By the hypothesis, 0 − B and A − (0 − B) are integer multiplicity whenever A and B are; the value of A − (0 − B) at ω is A(ω) + B(ω). Natural multiples kS follow by induction on k, and negative multiples as 0 − (|k|S). The finite combination follows by Finset.induction_on with Finset.sum_insert, starting from 0 by (a). The mass bound follows from the argument of (b) applied to the finite sum.
3. Hence the statement holds, and the accepted declaration is linked unchanged as this child. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reuse the comparator-accepted declaration cbr_cc_current_algebra with its identical frozen type.

subproblems.title: IMRep calculus: tangent locality, Borel restriction, differences, orientation bound (reuse of the accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement:
(a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q: M has approximate tangent space Q at x if and only if M' does (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).
(b) Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E Borel. Then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep R' in U, and it represents some current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
(c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B.
(d) For every IMRep R in any U and Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm).

This is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument of 1.6; Ch. 6, Remarks 2.6, 2.9 and 3.2(1). This theorem is reused verbatim, not re-proved.
1. The DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1 has status accepted. Its Lean declaration Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub passed the comparator with exactly this frozen type (byte-identical lean_statement) and only the standard axioms. It is already shared by several DAG branches and is the resolved dependency of the selected node.
2. Its accepted proof shows:
   (a) Hⁿ⌞(M' ∖ M) has zero n-density at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M, so at such points the blow-ups of M and M' have the same limits.
   (b) Every IMRep field restricts to the Borel set M ∩ E (the orientation field via (a)). The represented current is defined by the integral, and its sequential continuity follows from (d).
   (c) The two representations are combined on the union of the carriers, with integer multiplicities taken with signs relative to a common unit orientation on the overlap; two unit orientations of the same plane differ by a sign. This uses (a).
   (d) By the Cauchy–Binet formula, |α(τ₁, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ.
3. Hence the statement holds, and the accepted declaration is linked unchanged as this child. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reuse the comparator-accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub with its identical frozen type.
